item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
896
ABPZ20 KNHC 151730
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Thu Oct 15 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Simon, located a few hundred miles south-southeast of the
southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula, and on Hurricane
Trudy, located several hundred miles south-southwest of Acapulco,
Mexico.

South of Southern Mexico:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form offshore of southern
Mexico during the early to middle part of next week. Environmental
conditions appear conducive for gradual development thereafter, and
a tropical depression could form during the second half of next week
while the system moves generally westward to west-northwestward over
the east to central portion of the East Pacific.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...40 percent.

$$
Forecaster Papin

item.description:

BULLETIN
Hurricane Trudy Advisory Number  10
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
300 PM CST Thu Oct 15 2026
 
...HURRICANE WATCH AND TROPICAL STORM WARNING ISSUED FOR PORTIONS
OF THE COAST OF MEXICO...
...TRUDY EXPECTED TO RAPIDLY INTENSIFY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 300 PM CST...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...13.7N 101.7W
ABOUT 250 MI...405 KM SSW OF ACAPULCO MEXICO
ABOUT 405 MI...650 KM SSE OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...90 MPH...150 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NNW OR 345 DEGREES AT 6 MPH...9 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...978 MB...28.88 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
The Government of Mexico has issued a Hurricane Watch for the coast
of Mexico north of Punta San Telmo to Playa Perula.
 
The Government of Mexico has issued a Tropical Storm Warning for
the coast of Mexico from Punta San Telmo southward to Zihuatanejo.
 
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Hurricane Watch is in effect for...
* The coast of Mexico north of Punta San Telmo to Playa Perula.
 
A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for...
* The coast of Mexico from Punta San Telmo southward to Zihuatanejo.
 
A Hurricane Watch means that hurricane conditions are possible
within the watch area.  A watch is typically issued 48 hours
before the anticipated first occurrence of tropical-storm-force
winds, conditions that make outside preparations difficult or
dangerous.
 
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected somewhere within the warning area within 36 hours.
 
Interests elsewhere in southwestern and west-central Mexico should
continue monitor the progress of Trudy. Additional watches or
warnings will likely be required for portions of these areas later
today or tonight.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 300 PM CST (2100 UTC), the center of Hurricane Trudy was located
near latitude 13.7 North, longitude 101.7 West. Trudy is moving
toward the north-northwest near 6 mph (9 km/h). This motion is 
expected to continue through Friday, followed by a turn toward the 
northwest Friday night or Saturday.  On the forecast track the 
center of Trudy will approach the coast of southwestern and 
west-central Mexico on Saturday.
 
Trudy has changed little in strength during the past few hours, and 
maximum sustained winds are near 90 mph (150 km/h) with higher
gusts. Rapid intensification is forecast to resume tonight, and 
Trudy is forecast to become a major hurricane Friday or Friday 
night.

Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 25 miles (35 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 105 miles
(165 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 978 mb (28.88 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Trudy can be found in the Tropical Cyclone 
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP1 and WMO header WTPZ41 KNHC 
and on the web at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep1.shtml?key_messages.
 
WIND: Tropical storm conditions are expected within the tropical 
storm warning area area by early Saturday. Tropical storm conditions 
are expected to spread into the hurricane watch area on Saturday.
 
RAINFALL: Through the weekend, Trudy is expected to produce 4 to 8
inches with isolated higher totals around 12 inches through the
weekend along and near the southwest Mexican coast in Michoacán,
Colima and Jalisco. This rainfall may produce life-threatening
flooding and mudslides, especially in areas along steep terrain.
 
Elsewhere, Trudy’s outer bands are expected to produce 2 to 4
inches with isolated higher totals around 6 inches along the
southwest Mexican coast in Guerrero. This rainfall may result in
localized flash flooding through the weekend, especially in areas
along steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Trudy,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep1.shtml?rainqpf.
 
STORM SURGE: Coastal flooding from storm surge is possible in areas
of onshore winds. Near the coast, the surge will be accompanied by
large and destructive waves.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Trudy are expected to begin affecting
portions of the coast of southwestern Mexico over the next day or so
and continue through the weekend. These swells are likely to cause
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please consult
products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next intermediate advisory at 600 PM CST.
Next complete advisory at 900 PM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Beven

item.title: Hurricane Trudy Forecast Discussion Number 10
item.description:
Issued at 300 PM CST Thu Oct 15 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 152049
TCDEP1
 
Hurricane Trudy Discussion Number  10
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
300 PM CST Thu Oct 15 2026

Trudy's intensification appears to have temporarily paused. An Air 
Force Reserve Hurricane Hunter aircraft investigated the hurricane 
a few hours ago and reported maximum 700-mb flight-level winds of 
84 kt and a central pressure near 978 mb.  Satellite imagery shows 
an attempt to form an eye, but it has not yet fully cleared out. 
The various satellite intensity estimates have changed little over 
the past few hours, and the initial intensity remains 80 kt based 
on them and the aircraft data.  The satellite imagery suggests a 
tongue of dry air is wrapping into the cyclone around the north 
side of the central dense overcast, and this may be responsible for 
the pause in the development.

The initial motion is north-northwestward or 345/5 kt. The 
hurricane is currently heading for a weakness in the subtropical 
ridge caused by a mid- to upper-level trough extending from the 
Yucatan Peninsula westward to central Mexico. During the next 36 h, 
this feature should weaken and move eastward, allowing a mid- to 
upper-level ridge to develop over Mexico. This evolution should 
cause Trudy to turn northwestward roughly parallel to the coast of 
Mexico. The bulk of the track guidance keeps the center just 
offshore of the coast. However, any track to the right of the 
official forecast - such as shown by the GFS - would bring the 
center onshore. After 72 h, low- to mid-level ridging to the north 
of the cyclone should steer it slowly westward. The new track 
forecast is a little to the east of the previous forecast through 
36 h, similar to the previous forecast from 36-72 h, and a little 
north of the previous forecast from 72-120 h.

Except for the apparent tongue of dry air, conditions appear 
favorable for steady to rapid development during the next 24-36 h. 
The new intensity forecast keeps the peak intensity of 125 kt from 
the previous advisory, which is near or a little above the upper 
edge of the intensity guidance.  After 36 h, there should be 
increasing southwesterly shear that will likely halt development. 
Even with the forecast track keeping the center offshore, the 
cyclone will likely be close enough to land to cause the cyclone 
to weaken. However, any track to the left and farther offshore of 
the current forecast would let Trudy stay stronger than currently 
forecast, while any track that the brings the center inland would 
cause rapid weakening and possibly dissipation. Beyond 72 h, strong 
shear should cause continued weakening even though the center is 
moving away from land.  The intensity forecast follows the overall 
trend of the guidance, and it is near the upper edge of the 
guidance.
 
 
KEY MESSAGES:
 
1. Trudy is forecast to be a major hurricane as it approaches the 
coast of southwestern and west-central Mexico this weekend. There is 
an increasing risk of wind, rain, and storm surge impacts. A 
Hurricane Watch and a Tropical Storm Warning have been issued for a 
portion of the southwestern Mexican coast, and additional watches 
will likely be required further up the coast tonight or Friday.
 
2. Heavy rainfall associated with Trudy will impact the southwest 
Mexican coast between Guerrero and Jalisco through the weekend. This 
rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides by the 
weekend along and near the southwest Mexican coast in Michoacán, 
Colima, and Jalisco, especially in areas along steep terrain.
 
3. Large swells will begin to affect portions of the coast of
southwestern Mexico Friday and continue through the weekend. These
swells could cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS

 24H  16/1800Z 15.2N 102.2W  115 KT 130 MPH

item.description:
Issued at 200 PM MST Thu Oct 15 2026 
759 
WTPZ35 KNHC 152041

BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Simon Advisory Number  34
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
200 PM MST Thu Oct 15 2026
 
...SMALL SIMON SLOWLY WEAKENING AS IT DRIFTS NORTHWESTWARD...
...NOW FORECAST TO BECOME A REMNANT LOW IN A COUPLE OF DAYS...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 PM MST...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...19.3N 108.2W
ABOUT 270 MI...435 KM SSE OF CABO SAN LUCAS MEXICO
ABOUT 180 MI...290 KM WSW OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...50 MPH...85 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 325 DEGREES AT 1 MPH...2 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...999 MB...29.50 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests in Baja California Sur should continue to monitor Simon.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 PM MST (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Simon was 
located near latitude 19.3 North, longitude 108.2 West. Simon is 
moving toward the northwest near 1 mph (2 km/h). A faster 
northwestward motion is forecast to begin by Friday and continue 
through the weekend.
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to near 50 mph (85 km/h) with 
higher gusts. Gradual weakening is expected during the next few 
days, and Simon is forecast to become a post-tropical remnant low by 
this weekend.
 
Simon is a small tropical cyclone. Tropical-storm-force winds extend 
outward up to 45 miles (75 km) from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 999 mb (29.50 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Simon can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP5 and WMO header WTPZ45 KNHC
and on the web at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep5.shtml?key_messages.
 
RAINFALL: Through early Saturday, Simon is expected to produce
rainfall totals of 1 to 2 inches with isolated maximum amounts of 3
inches over portions of the state of Baja California Sur.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Simon,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep5.shtml?rainqpf.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Simon could affect portions of the coast 
of west-central Mexico and Baja California Sur during the next day 
or so. These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and 
rip current conditions. Please consult products from your local 
weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 PM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Papin

NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
200 PM MST Thu Oct 15 2026

Simon continues to produce an area of deep convection, though this 
activity has lacked a ton of organization today, and appears to 
still be displaced to the west of the center of circulation. A RCM-2 
synthetic aperture radar (SAR) pass that became available after the 
prior advisory indicated that most of this convective activity was 
also occurring outside of its radius of maximum winds, and has done 
little to aid the small circulation. In fact, the peak winds 
retrieved from the SAR was only 47 kt. This information, combined 
with a Metop-B scatterometer pass that had a peak wind of 39 kt is 
justification to bring Simon's intensity down to 45 kt this 
advisory, and this may still be generous. 

Simon has been drifting rather aimlessly today, and my best guess 
at an estimated motion is 320/1 kt. It has been a tough few days 
trying to forecast Simon's track, but the model guidance this cycle 
is finally coming into better agreement showing that as Simon 
becomes a more vertically shallow cyclone, it will primarily be 
steered by the low-level flow. To that end, a weak low-level trough 
is forecast to drop equatorward to the west of Simon as a strong 
pressure gradient develops over northern Mexico as surface ridging 
builds in behind a frontal boundary. This flow should help to 
finally draw Simon back to the northwest with a speed up in its 
forward motion. The latest NHC track forecast is shifted once again 
a little further west but also faster, following the latest trends 
in the reliable HFIP Corrected Consensus Approach (HCCA) and Google 
DeepMind ensemble mean (GDMI). 

While the shear over Simon is currently low, it has not taken 
advantage of these more favorable conditions, likely due to the 
proximity of dry air preventing the convection from organizing. The 
vertical wind shear is soon expected to increase significantly out 
of the southwest as a deep-layer trough located over the 
southwestern United States cuts off and retrogrades back westward. 
Simon has already been sensitive to less than pristine conditions, 
and this increase in shear will likely be the storm's demise. The 
latest NHC forecast now shows gradual weakening continuing over the 
next 24-36 h, with Simon becoming a remnant low in 48 h, and fully 
dissipating in 72 h. If the latest ECMWF forecast is correct, this 
could occur sooner than forecasted here.
